QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_6

question.text: Mr. Arjun Kulkarni, CFO of Narmada Cat II AIF (a SEBI-registered trust), asks which India tax form is used to pass through income details to unit-holders so they can report their share in their personal returns under the Section 115UB pass-through regime:

answer.text: Form 64C — statement of income distributed to unit-holders

explanation.text: The Logic: For Category I and II AIF pass-through taxation, the statement of income paid or credited to unit-holders is furnished in Form No. 64C by 30 June of the following financial year. The fund separately furnishes Form No. 64D to the tax authority by 15 June. Form 64C is therefore the unit-holder facing pass-through statement under the Section 115UB regime. The Trap: Form 15G is a TDS waiver self-declaration for resident individuals. Form 26AS is the income-tax department's annual tax-credit statement. Form 3CEB relates to transfer-pricing-reportable international transactions and is irrelevant to AIF pass-through reporting. Note: Source pages 446-447 and 466 support Form 64C as the unit-holder statement, the 30 June deadline, and the separate Form 64D filing by 15 June.
